newsitem.title: USA: Two Illinois incinerator lawsuits consolidated.
newsitem.headline: Two Illinois incinerator lawsuits consolidated.

text.p: A Cook County, Ill., Circuit Court judge Friday consolidated for pre-trial purposes two lawsuits brought against the state of Illinois by incinerator developers.

Rick Redmond, a Chicago attorney representing state officials, said Judge Arthur Dunne granted the state's request to consolidate lawsuits brought by Foster Wheeler Corp and CGE Ford Heights and CGE Fulton after attorneys for the developers agreed to unite the lawsuits for pre-trial purposes only.
Redmond said the pre-trial in the cases would involve the state's pending motions to dismiss both lawsuits, as well as requests for summary judgement.
He added that a status on the cases was expected soon before Judge Robert Boharic.

Foster Wheeler filed the lawsuit constesting the legality of Illinois' repeal of a state subsidy for a waste-to-energy incinerator it developed in Robbins after the company's original lawsuit was dismissed Nov. 1 in U.S. District Court in Chicago.
The company also appealed the dismissal to the U.S. Appeals Court, where action on the appeal has been stayed pending resolution of the lawsuit in county court.

The CGE case was filed in county court shortly after Gov. Jim Edgar last March signed the repeal into law revoking the state's guarentee that the incinerators could sell electricity they produced to utilities at a higher rate.
Nearly $500 million of unrated, tax-exempt debt that was largely dependent on the state subsidy had been sold by the developers to finance projects in Robbins, Ford Heights and Fulton.
